venue.name: Butchart Gardens – National Historic Site
venue.description: The Butchart Gardens is a 122-year-old, 55-acre display garden in Brentwood Bay, created by Jennie Butchart and still privately owned and operated by the family. It was designated a National Historic Site of Canada in 2004. The site is open year round with seasonal hours and seasonal admission rates, and includes the Sunken, Rose, Japanese, Italian and Mediterranean Gardens, a Rose Carousel, four food service locations and a Seed & Gift Store. Visits are self-guided; the Gardens do not offer or permit guided tours.
venue.address: 800 Benvenuto Avenue, Brentwood Bay, BC V8M 1J8

facility_notes.washrooms: All washroom facilities have a large stall for wheelchair access. Some entrances have electric push-button doors for easy entry. All of the washrooms on the grounds are outfitted with baby changing stations. A parent room is located near the Rose Carousel building and in the visitor parking lot.
facility_notes.lunch_space: There are some picnic tables located close to our Information Centre year-round. Additionally, we add some picnic tables in the green spaces of our parking lots (usually June for the summer months). Picnicking on the grassy areas/lawns within the Gardens is not permitted except on the Concert Lawn and Fireworks Viewing Lawn.
facility_notes.rain_backup: If it rains – or will rain imminently! – our staff distribute hundreds of umbrellas throughout the grounds and parking lots so you can borrow one and stay dry.
facility_notes.stroller_accessible: Complimentary strollers are available with a refundable deposit, on a first-come, first-served basis from the Visitor Centre. Pull wagons are not permitted as they cause congestion on our pathways.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: Some pathways are narrow and there are pathways with a steeper grade; alternate routes are noted by signage and on the visitor map. The two locations in The Gardens that are not wheelchair or scooter accessible are The Mound and The Wharf.
facility_notes.bus_parking: All parking is free. We do not permit overnight parking. We accommodate cars, bicycles and RVs. Accessible parking for those with disabilities is also available.

restrictions: We do not offer or permit guided tours of The Gardens
No backpacks permitted in The Gardens except for medical reason
Groups are not permitted to participate in scavenger hunts as they are too disruptive to other visitors
No running, no catching or throwing games
Music, musical instruments, and performances of any kind are not permitted
BBQs of any kind are not permitted
The entire property, including parking lots, is smoke-free and vapour-free
Pull wagons are not permitted, however push wagons are allowed
venue.hours_notes: The hours listed reflect admission gate times; The Gardens are open for viewing one hour after the gates close. Summer 2026 (June 1 – September 15): Monday–Tuesday 9:00am–5:00pm, Wednesday–Sunday 9:00am–10:00pm. September 16–30: 9:00am–5:00pm daily.
venue.seasonal_notes: Open year round with seasonal hours and rates. Autumn (October) 9:00am–4:00pm, November 9:00am–3:30pm, Christmas (December 1 – January 6) 3:00pm–9:00pm and closed December 25, Winter (January 7 – March 31) 9:00am–3:30pm or 4:00pm, closed January 18–31 for staff holiday, Spring (April–May) 9:00am–5:00pm.
venue.price_year_or_season: 2026–2027 seasonal rates from the Hours & Rates page (last modified 2026-06-24); the general admission figures recorded here are the Summer 2026 rates for June 1 – September 15.

programs.name: School group field trip (self-guided)
programs.description: Organized school groups and field trips are welcomed October 15 – April 15 only; no school field trips are accepted after April 16. Advance reservations are required and based on availability. Visits are restricted to a maximum of two hours and a maximum of 60 students. Child and youth seasonal rates apply: the child (5–12) rate is $3.00 including tax for October, November, January to March and April, and $5.00 during the Christmas season (December 1 – January 6); youth aged 13–17 pay the higher youth rate, which ranges from $12.60 to $21.13 across the same months. The Gardens are closed December 25 and January 18–31. All chaperones must read and sign the School Group & Field Trip Policy form before arrival.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the main pathways in units of ten or fewer with an adult, staying on the paths and talking quietly, past the Sunken, Rose, Japanese, Italian and Mediterranean gardens. A leisurely full circuit is about 1.5 kilometres and takes most visitors 1.5 to 2 hours.
programs.our_note: The two-hour cap and the walking distance are the same number, so there is no slack in the visit — plan one loop and skip the gift shop. The Gardens describe themselves as a private display garden and not a playground, and they explicitly rule out running, throwing games and scavenger hunts, so this suits a group that is already comfortable walking quietly. The window closes hard on April 15, which is a fortnight before the tulips peak.
programs.practical_summary: Free parking, washrooms with change tables throughout, and picnic tables by the Information Centre; the whole visit is outdoors and the rain plan is borrowed umbrellas. The public FAQ and the school group policy disagree about whether packed lunches can be eaten on site, so confirm when you book.
programs.extra_fees_note: Rates are seasonal. The $3.00 child rate applies in October, November, January–March and April; the child rate is $5.00 during the Christmas season, December 1 – January 6. Youth aged 13–17 pay the youth rate for the season.

programs.name: Child and youth group visit (self-guided)
programs.description: Child and youth groups other than school field trips are taken year round. Advance reservations are required and based on availability. Child and youth seasonal rates apply; the child (5–12) rate recorded here is the Summer 2026 rate of $5.00 including tax, and falls to $3.00 in October, November and January to April. Chaperones are required at 1 adult per 10 students and receive complimentary admission on that ratio. All chaperones must read and sign the Youth Group Policies before arrival. No maximum group size or visit length is published for this category.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the garden paths in units of ten or fewer with an adult, staying on the paths, past the Sunken, Rose, Japanese, Italian and Mediterranean gardens; a leisurely circuit is about 1.5 kilometres.
programs.our_note: This is the route to ask about if your dates fall outside the October-to-April school window, and unlike the school category it carries no published two-hour limit or 60-child cap — but that also means nothing is guaranteed until Group Services confirms it. Summer rates are the highest of the year, so an autumn or winter date costs a child $3 rather than $5.
programs.practical_summary: Free parking, washrooms with baby change tables and a parent room, complimentary strollers from the Visitor Centre, and picnic tables near the Information Centre. There is no indoor space to retreat to and no published limit on group size — both worth asking about.
programs.extra_fees_note: Rates are seasonal and change through the year: the child (5–12) rate is $5.00 in summer and at Christmas and $3.00 in autumn, winter and spring. Youth aged 13–17 pay the youth rate for the season.

images.alt: A stone pathway leads through a garden flanked by large, flowering shrubs that appear to be Hydrangea paniculata, featuring creamy white blooms. In the centre, a bronze dragon sculpture is positioned in front of a stone wall, surrounded by colourful flower beds with pink and yellow blooms. Lush green trees and plants provide a vibrant backdrop

gaps: age range: the Gardens publish no minimum or maximum age for school or youth groups, only the 5–12 child and 13–17 youth admission bands, so age_basis is left null rather than inferred from ticket categories.
lead time: 'Advanced reservations are required and based on availability' — no minimum notice period in days is published.
capacity: no maximum group size is published for the child and youth group category (the 60-student cap is stated only for school field trips), and no minimum group size is published for either.
deposit and payment timing: not published for group visits.
cancellation: no cancellation or weather policy for groups is published; the only refund statement covers individual online tickets.
lunch space: no indoor space is available to a group, and the two picnic tables near the Information Centre are the only year-round tables.
rain backup: there is no indoor alternative — the published rain plan is borrowed umbrellas.
hosts_daycare_groups is recorded true on the strength of the separate 'Child & Youth Groups' category; the site sets no floor age, so whether a preschool group is accepted is not actually stated.
The 'Book Your Group Visit' form on the Groups page is a JS-rendered form; its fields were readable but no confirmation of what happens after submission is published.
The Groups page links two different Youth Group Policies PDFs (a 2026 version in the Child & Youth section and a 2024 version under Planning Resources); the 2026 version was used.
The homepage og:image (Homepage-hero.jpg) carries no alt attribute, so the hero was taken from the Hours & Rates page, where the photo has a full descriptive alt written by the site.
